newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA C.BANK CHANGES CURRENCY FIXING CALCULATION.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA C.BANK CHANGES CURRENCY FIXING CALCULATION.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said on Monday it will base calculations of daily currency fixings on interbank volumes higher than $10 million sold and $10 million bought.
The decision, effective from Monday, was taken "to achieve a more realistic reflection of the interbank foreign exchange market and its relation to traded volumes," said a BNB statement.
The lev, under pressure due to delayed reforms and a collapsing financial system, lost 33 percent of its value against the dollar in the first several days of this year.
Bulgaria's illiquid interbank foreign exchange market is moved by to low levels by small volumes.
On January 3, when the lev collapsed from 510 to the dollar to 600, interbank forex market turnover was $7.19 million.
The lev/dollar fixing for Tuesday remained unchanged at 581.78 per dollar after the BNB reported $9.4 million bought and $7.87 million sold on Monday on the local market.
The lev tested 700 to the dollar on the local forex market but firmed at close to around 680 on rising dollar sales by small firms. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
